sections.h2: Choices for a fast sale in Port Arthur
sections.html:
Sellers here can take a cash offer, hire an agent, or sell the house as is. Old storm damage, postponed upkeep and title questions are the usual triggers for a direct sale.

Cash skips the lender's appraisal and the repair list that can follow it. A listing may reach a higher price if the house is sound and you can wait for a financed buyer. Whichever you choose, get price, date and costs in writing.

  • Direct sale: storm wear, tenants, liens and estates.
  • Listing: sound houses and flexible timelines.
  • Collect repair receipts and flood claim records early, since buyers and insurers ask.

sections.h2: Port Arthur's neighborhoods and housing eras
sections.html:
Arthur E. Stilwell began platting the city on Sabine Lake's west shore in 1895, and incorporation came in 1898. Spindletop erupted on January 10, 1901, refineries followed from Gulf in 1901 and Texaco in 1902, and the population reached 56,039 in 2020.

Griffing Park, Pear Ridge and Lakeview were absorbed over the years and still go by those names. Sabine Pass and Port Acres are often seen as separate, and Sabine Pass has its own school district, water district, port authority and ZIP code. Check which taxing units serve your address.

The housing reflects several eras: refinery-boom neighborhoods near downtown, communities folded in later, and newer homes built after the 2017 storm. Describe your own house's era accurately.

Port Arthur dates that shaped its housing
DateWhat happened
1895Platting begins on Sabine Lake
1898Incorporated as a city
January 10, 1901Spindletop erupts
1931Neches River Rainbow Bridge completed
2017Hurricane Harvey damages the housing stock

Expect to explain it. FEMA estimated that 80% of Port Arthur's housing was damaged or destroyed in August 2017.

HUD and state disaster funds went to buyouts, rehabilitation and new construction. If your house took water, buyers will ask what was fixed, by whom and under which permits.

  • Pull invoices, permits and inspection reports.
  • Keep flood insurance or FEMA claim papers.
  • If a recovery program helped you, ask its office whether any conditions stay with the property.

Recovery programs aimed at buyers with incomes between 80% and 120% of area median income, so a market of subsidized new homes now sits beside older stock. Buyers will compare yours with both, so call the city's housing office for the rules that apply today.

By 1950 five refineries in the area employed about 12,000 workers, whose pay accounted for half of all money spent in Port Arthur stores. Oil Workers union membership reached roughly 8,000 in 1948, and union influence declined somewhat from the mid-1970s.

The canal that built the port also cut the city off from Sabine Lake. Pleasure Island, an 18.5-mile land mass built from dredged earth, gave the city a second chance at tourism. The Neches River Rainbow Bridge on State Highway 87, completed in 1931, is 230 feet tall and links Port Arthur with Orange.

A roller coaster and dance hall went up on the island in 1913. A barge struck and burned the connecting bridge in 1967, and the Gulfgate Bridge was built afterward. Those layers of history mean buyers see a mix of older refinery-era houses and newer infill, so say which one yours is.

Value is set as of January 1, and the year's lien attaches then. Whoever buys inherits any unpaid balance unless the title company clears it.

Statements are mailed near October 1 and turn delinquent after January 31. A homestead earns a $140,000 school exemption, and a senior or disabled owner adds $60,000 and a ceiling on school tax. A disabled veteran takes $5,000 to $12,000 off by rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a full exemption. Protests are generally due May 15.

Get a payoff from the Jefferson County tax office before signing a contract. Several taxing units can appear on one bill, so check each line against your address.

Most of the city is in Jefferson County, though a small part reaches into Orange County. Ask which county holds your parcel before the deed is drafted.

To be recorded, a deed needs your signature and a notary's acknowledgment. Clerk fees start at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 per extra page, with records charges on top.

For an inherited house, the route depends on the estate: an executor's deed, a muniment of title order, a recorded transfer on death deed or an affidavit of heirship.

Texas clocks run short. A default notice leaves 20 days to pay the arrears, and the lender must give 21 days' notice before a first-Tuesday auction.

A deficiency suit after a sale must be filed within two years, and a former owner has two years to claim surplus from a tax foreclosure. A will can generally be probated within four years of death, and a small estate affidavit may suit assets of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

  • Storm damage: sell as is when repairs would cost more than they add.
  • Back taxes: ask the collector about an installment plan.
  • Estate: confirm who may sign before accepting an offer.

sections.h2: Papers and questions before you accept
sections.html:
Gather the deed, your latest tax statement, any flood insurance or FEMA claim papers and the payoff contact at your lender. If tenants live there, add the lease and deposit record. For an inherited house, bring the court or estate papers that show who may sign.

Ask each buyer who pays for the title policy, how many days closing takes and whether the price can drop after a walkthrough. Skip anyone who asks for money up front or will not write terms down. If the house has storm repairs, open permits or a lien, mention it on the first call, because buyers who discover it late tend to cut the offer.

Compare offers by what you keep. Deduct commissions, repairs, carrying costs and title charges from each price, then line up the totals. Ask each buyer for proof of funds, the earnest money amount and the closing date in writing.

After you accept, the title company searches for liens, orders tax figures and sets the signing. Bring photo ID and every key. Payoffs and taxes come out of the price and the balance is yours once the deed is recorded. Never pay a fee just to receive an offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a storm-damaged house in Port Arthur as is?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase damaged houses without repairs. Expect questions about flood history and permits, and collect invoices, claim records and any recovery-program paperwork first.

faqs.q: Is part of Port Arthur outside Jefferson County?
faqs.a: A small portion extends into Orange County. Confirm your parcel's county with the title company before the deed is prepared.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if Port Arthur taxes are late?
faqs.a: Bills unpaid after January 31 start drawing a six percent penalty and one percent interest on February 1. The penalty keeps rising until July 1.

faqs.q: Is there a time limit to probate a will in Texas?
faqs.a: Generally four years from death, though a court may accept a later filing for good cause. Small estates may use an affidavit instead if assets are $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

faqs.q: Is Sabine Pass a separate place from Port Arthur?
faqs.a: It is often seen as separate, with its own school district, water district, port authority and ZIP code. Check which taxing units serve your address.
